item.content:encoded:
Beginning to show it's age around the edges, but not all that bad. The paragraph about distributing plants grown within outside of the greenhouse is rather dated at this point (for all the standard lolFoundation tones it carries) and has almost no relation to the rest of the SCP, and ending with [DATA EXPUNGED] is of course a needless cliche.

That said, it's a nice case of morality that, while strange to us, can be completely rationalized within the minds of those doing it, so I'll upvote for that.

item.content:encoded:
This kind of mood whiplash is probably my favorite type of SCP - the cute/fluffy/cuddly stuff that suddenly becomes very creepy/nasty/scary. The inadvertent aspect of it just makes it that much better. The Little Shop of Horrors reference is nice, and not out of place the way most pop-culture references tend to be.

Upvoting despite some flaws in the writing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I think the idea for this is somewhat neat, but "sentience" is misused, I don't know how I feel about the reference to Little Shop of Horrors, and my downvote was sealed by two questions; why were they seeding these around a civilian town, and what the hell was the lead researcher's daughter doing in an SCP's containment area? Coupled with the lazy expungement at the end and the cheap horror, no thanks.

E: I misread stuff that led to the crossed out stuff in my comment, I apologise, but the rest of my critique stands, in my opinion.

item.title: Killing sentient organisms over a botanist
item.content:encoded: These things didn't understand what had happened,and the there was only one who did it!Dr Kingsley should NOT have been allowed to work with his daughter on the same SCP for psychological reasons,and the ivy should have been the only killed plant,and have other ivy monitored,along with having robots work with the plants,or explain to them all that humans are not to be "picked"like plants.also,the ivy was probably insane,as a flower would be a plant,so comparing severing a girl's head to picking a flower should show that the ivy has murderous instincts.kingsley,or SOMEONE should have realized this,but do to kingsley's position,he was able to act out of anger,killing sentient organisms(or SCP products in general)for no reason.and if they really are such a threat,just send in robots!there are many SCP's that have killed researchers intentionally before,and have very little consequence(like no food for a day).the whole murder thing was a dumb attempt to make this nice SCP seem scary,but it was completely unnecessary,as some can end happily.aside from the whole thing with the genocide,this was good.but this kinda ruined it,it my opinion.-1 Sorry if this was really long.

item.content:encoded:
Alright, monkeyed with the picture and the full size can be seen by right-clicking and Viewing Image

Also to clarify ahead of time, I added the tag "sympathetic" not because the plants were nice and sweet but because the core behavior of this SCP is that it affected the world around it and the plants within it in a sympathetic manner. When things were good in the greenhouse, things were good in the whole neighborhood. Likewise the plants were just as nurturing and kind as their gardeners — which unfortunately meant they weren't above pruning the research staff when they felt like it.
